rationale: The Newcastle Parkinson trial used dried sage-leaf capsules and specified a cognitive primary endpoint. Its secondary assessment schedule and any facial-expression outcome remain unverified. Mouse extract behavior is a different endpoint and supplies no directional facial-expression result.

The original military study distinguishes 106 agreeing to participate from 78 allocated to the omega-3 or corn-ester groups. Its original Epworth analysis details remain inaccessible and the cohort and comparator do not fit the claim. The Parkinson CBD study used a corn-oil comparator, and another registered comparison has retracted results. No comparison isolates refined corn oil.

The 30-participant registry describes brief induced oral pain with a C60-in-grapeseed comparator and no posted results or verified pressing grade. The earlier lab use of a similar material does not establish product identity or a pain result. Topical and preclinical contexts do not isolate oral cold-pressed grapeseed oil in Parkinson disease.
